target: Badan saya lemas dan kepala saya pusing seperti berputar.
english: My body is weak and my head is dizzy, like it's spinning.
tip: Pusing covers both dizzy and stressed-out: kepala saya pusing = my head is spinning.

target: Gigi bungsunya harus dicabut karena tumbuh miring dan menekan gigi lain.
english: His wisdom tooth has to be pulled because it grows crooked and presses on the other teeth.
tip: Gigi bungsu = wisdom tooth, literally 'youngest-child tooth': dicabut = gets pulled.

target: Mata minus saya bertambah karena terlalu sering menatap layar ponsel.
english: My nearsightedness has gotten worse because I stare at my phone screen too often.
tip: Mata minus = nearsighted, said with the number: minus saya bertambah = my prescription got worse.

target: Ayah memakai kacamata baca setiap kali membuka koran pagi.
english: Dad puts on his reading glasses every time he opens the morning paper.
tip: Kacamata = glasses, literally kaca (glass) + mata (eye): kacamata baca = reading glasses.

target: Kalau badan pegal dan meriang, orang Indonesia bilang kamu sedang masuk angin.
english: When your body is achy and feverish, Indonesians say you have 'masuk angin'.
tip: Masuk angin ('wind got in') = the classic catch-all unwellness: chills, bloating, fatigue. Untranslatable.

target: Penjual jamu gendong masih lewat depan rumah kami setiap pagi.
english: The traveling jamu seller still passes in front of our house every morning.
tip: Jamu gendong = jamu sold by a walking vendor carrying bottles in a back sling (gendong = carry on the back).

target: Minum air kelapa muda katanya bagus untuk meredakan panas dalam.
english: Drinking young coconut water is said to be good for soothing 'panas dalam'.
tip: Panas dalam ('inner heat') = folk ailment behind sore throats and canker sores; cooled with kelapa muda.

target: Dokter kami tidak melarang kerokan, asal kulitnya tidak sampai terluka.
english: Our doctor doesn't forbid kerokan, as long as the skin doesn't get injured.
tip: Asal = as long as (condition): asal kulit tidak terluka = as long as the skin isn't hurt.

target: Semoga cepat sembuh, ya, kabari kami kalau perlu bantuan apa pun.
english: Get well soon, okay? Let us know if you need any help at all.
tip: Semoga cepat sembuh is the standard get-well line, literally 'hopefully quickly recover'. Semoga starts most wishes: semoga sukses, semoga lancar.

target: Ibu titip salam dan doa untuk tantemu yang sedang sakit.
english: Mom sends her greetings and prayers for your aunt who is sick.
tip: Titip salam = pass greetings through someone: ibu titip salam = mom sends her regards.

target: Tetangga datang membawa sup hangat waktu anak saya sakit demam berdarah.
english: The neighbors came bringing warm soup when my child was sick with dengue fever.
tip: News and clinics shorten demam berdarah to DBD – three-letter abbreviations are everywhere in Indonesian, from KTP to SD.

target: Setelah menikah, mereka pindah dari kamar kos ke rumah kontrakan dua kamar.
english: After getting married, they moved from a boarding room to a two-bedroom rented house.
tip: Kontrakan = a whole house you rent, usually yearly; kos = just a room: rumah kontrakan = rented house.

target: Anak kos biasanya memasak sendiri di akhir bulan supaya lebih hemat.
english: Boarding-house kids usually cook for themselves at the end of the month to be more thrifty.
tip: Anak kos means a boarding-house renter, and it connotes a tight budget: masakan anak kos = cheap cooking. Hence memasak sendiri at the end of the month.

target: Listrik di rumah kami pakai token, jadi harus diisi sebelum habis.
english: The electricity at our house uses tokens, so it has to be topped up before it runs out.
tip: Token = prepaid electricity credit: beli token listrik = buy a code and punch it into the meter.

target: Kalau mati lampu, kami menyalakan lilin dan mengobrol di teras.
english: When the power goes out, we light candles and chat on the porch.
tip: Mati lampu = a power cut of any kind, not just the lamps: sedang mati lampu = the power is out.

target: Mereka membeli motor baru dengan DP tiga juta dan cicilan dua tahun.
english: They bought a new motorbike with a three-million down payment and two years of installments.
tip: DP (say de-pe) = down payment: DP tiga juta = a three-million down payment. Also called uang muka.

target: Toko itu menawarkan cicilan tanpa bunga untuk pembelian di atas satu juta.
english: That store offers installments without interest for purchases above one million.
tip: Bunga = flower AND interest: cicilan tanpa bunga = zero-interest installments.

target: Arisan ibu-ibu di kompleks kami berkumpul setiap tanggal lima belas.
english: The neighborhood mothers' arisan in our complex gathers on the fifteenth of every month.
tip: An arisan is a rotating savings club: everyone pays in each round, one member takes the whole pot, and the rotation runs until all have had a turn.

target: Nama ibu keluar waktu arisan dikocok, lumayan untuk membayar uang sekolah adik.
english: Mom's name came out when the arisan was drawn — helpful for paying my younger sibling's school fees.
tip: Dikocok = shaken up and drawn by lot: nama ibu keluar = mom's name came out, she wins this round.

target: Setiap arisan selesai, ibu-ibu masih duduk lama membahas harga sembako.
english: Every time the arisan is over, the mothers still sit around a long time discussing staple food prices.
tip: Sembako is short for sembilan bahan pokok – the nine staple goods (rice, oil, sugar and so on). Harga sembako = the price of the basics everyone tracks.

target: Gaji di kantor kami cair setiap tanggal dua puluh lima, langsung dipotong iuran.
english: The salary at our office comes through on the twenty-fifth, with dues deducted right away.
tip: Cair, literally liquid = money comes through: gajinya sudah cair = the salary has landed.

target: Belanja bulanan tanpa daftar ujung-ujungnya penuh barang yang tidak penting.
english: A monthly shop without a list ends up full of unimportant stuff.
tip: Ujung means 'end'; doubled, ujung-ujungnya is literally 'at its very ends' = 'it always ends up': ujung-ujungnya penuh barang yang tidak penting.

target: Harga cabai naik lagi, Bu? Rasanya kemarin masih setengah dari ini.
english: Chili prices are up again, ma'am? I feel like yesterday it was still half this much.
tip: Chili prices swing constantly and everyone tracks them – harga cabai naik lagi? is genuine national small talk at any market stall.

target: Saya memilih toko yang lebih jauh karena ongkirnya gratis.
english: I chose the store that is farther away because its shipping is free.
tip: Ongkir = ongkos kirim, the delivery fee; plain ongkos is a transport fare: gratis ongkir = free shipping.

target: Kami menabung sedikit demi sedikit untuk biaya kuliah anak nanti.
english: We are saving little by little for the children's future college costs.
tip: Demi builds 'X by X' phrases: sedikit demi sedikit = little by little, satu demi satu = one by one. The doubling marks slow, steady progress.

target: Tukang parkir di pasar sekarang juga menerima pembayaran lewat dompet digital.
english: The parking attendants at the market now also accept payment through digital wallets.
tip: Tukang = the ... guy, by trade: tukang parkir = parking attendant, tukang galon = the water guy.

target: Mengisi saldo di minimarket biasanya kena biaya tambahan seribu rupiah.
english: Topping up a balance at the minimart usually incurs an extra fee of one thousand rupiah.
tip: Kena means 'get hit by' something unwelcome: kena biaya = get charged a fee, kena hujan = get rained on, kena macet = get stuck in traffic.

target: Tukang itu membawa palu, obeng, dan gergaji di dalam kotak peralatannya.
english: That handyman carries a hammer, a screwdriver, and a saw in his toolbox.
tip: On its own, tukang means a handyman – the tukang with his palu and gergaji. Add a trade and it names the specialist: tukang kayu = carpenter.

target: Paku di dinding ini sudah berkarat, jadi harus diganti dengan yang baru.
english: The nail in this wall has rusted, so it has to be replaced with a new one.
tip: ber- + noun = 'to have/produce it': karat rust, berkarat rusty; debu dust, berdebu dusty.

target: Sebelum mengecat tembok, tutup lantai dengan plastik supaya tidak kotor.
english: Before painting the wall, cover the floor with plastic so it doesn't get dirty.
tip: One-syllable roots take menge-: cat, mengecat = to paint; cas, mengecas = to charge.
